tasks.short: Search journals and newsletters for developments, read current literature, talk with colleagues, and take part in education and conferences.

steps.what: Patient representative searches journals and newsletters for developments in the field
Patient representative talks with colleagues about developments
Patient representative participates in professional organizations and conferences

tasks.design: Saved searches and newsletter subscriptions are routed into one reading list by topic ({OTHER}), so the representative does not visit each source. Reading, talking with colleagues and conferences stay with the representative.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each journal and newsletter was checked separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and feed readers gather sources in one list.
tasks.still_hard: Conference news is not in the feeds.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from peers how a new complaints rule works in practice.

evidence.claim: Saved searches and feed readers can gather sources in one reading list.

assumptions: Boundary: from field developments to the conference attended; own research is outside.
Input contract: sources offer alerts or feeds; fallback is visiting each.
Reading and conferences do not change.

incremental.description: Patient representative sets up and tunes saved searches.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few sources; high: many journals and newsletters.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Log patient complaints and contacts, count and group cases for the report, analyse patterns and write recommendations, check the report, and send it to the quality committee.

steps.what: Patient representative logs patient encounters and complaints in a spreadsheet
Patient representative counts and groups cases to collect data for the report
Patient representative analyses patterns and writes recommendations for change
Patient representative checks the final report
Patient representative e-mails the report to the quality committee

tasks.design: Complaints and contacts are logged in a complaint workflow app ({WORKFLOW}) with fixed categories, department and deadline, so they are not kept in a spreadsheet. A dashboard ({BI}) counts and groups cases by category, department and outcome per period, so the representative does not tally them. Analysing patterns and writing recommendations stay with the representative. Once checked, the report goes to the quality committee from the dashboard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contacts were logged in spreadsheets and tallied by hand for each report.
tasks.enabler_now: Complaint workflow apps with categories feed dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Categories do not fit every complaint.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that three small complaints point to one unsafe practice.
tasks.altitude: The representative analyses instead of tallying.

evidence.claim: Complaint workflow apps with categories and deadlines can feed dashboards.
Care providers must run a complaints procedure with set rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient contact to the report sent; changes in care are outside.
Input contract: categories agreed with the quality committee; fallback is the spreadsheet.

incremental.description: Patient representative reviews categories each year.

approvals.approved_version: The report as checked by the representative in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few complaints; high: large hospitals with many contacts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect income documents from the patient, compute the sliding-scale tier, decide on exceptions, explain the charge, and record the decision.

steps.what: Patient representative collects income documents from patients
Patient representative analyzes patients' abilities to pay in a spreadsheet
Patient representative determines charges on a sliding scale and decides exceptions
Patient representative explains the charge to the patient
Patient representative records the decision in the billing system

tasks.design: Patients upload income documents through the patient portal instead of bringing them in. Fixed sliding-scale rules in the billing system ({OTHER}) compute the tier from household size and income, so the representative does not calculate it in a spreadsheet; the representative confirms every tier and decides exceptions, and the confirmed tier is stored on the account. Explaining the charge stays with the representative.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents were brought in on paper and tiers calculated in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Billing systems compute tiers by fixed rules; portals take document uploads.
tasks.still_hard: Self-employed patients' income is hard to prove.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing hardship that the income figures do not show.
tasks.altitude: The representative decides exceptions instead of calculating.

reach.learn: Whether tiers are set before billing.

evidence.claim: Billing systems can compute sliding-scale tiers by fixed rules from household size and income.
Decisions with significant effects may not rest solely on automated processing; the representative confirms each tier.

assumptions: Boundary: from the payment request to the decision recorded; debt collection is outside.
Input contract: sliding-scale rules set by the hospital; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Patients upload documents in about the time bringing them took; a little patient time is priced.
Every tier is confirmed by the representative.
research_questions: Are tiers set before the first invoice more often?

incremental.description: Patient representative helps patients who cannot upload documents.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many self-employed patients; high: mostly salaried patients with clear documents.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan sources for research and recommendations on liability, risk and quality, select relevant items, write summaries, check the newsletter, and share it with staff.

steps.what: Patient representative scans sources to identify research on legal liabilities and quality of care
Patient representative selects relevant research and recommendations
Patient representative writes summaries for the risk management newsletter

loop.output: A short summary per source with its link.
loop.check: Every sentence must match a passage in the source or it is dropped; the representative edits every summary.
loop.stop: One draft per source; if nothing passes, the representative writes the summary.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each source differs; a template cannot summarise it.

steps.what: Patient representative checks the final newsletter
Patient representative shares the newsletter with staff by e-mail

tasks.design: Alerts from the inspectorate, professional bodies, journals and case law sites arrive in one reading list ({OTHER}), so sources are not scanned one by one. For the selected items, a bounded step drafts short summaries from the source text; sentences that do not match the source are dropped, and the representative edits every summary. Once checked, the newsletter goes to staff through the intranet mailing list. Selecting what matters stays with the representative.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each source was scanned separately and every summary written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Feeds gather sources; language models draft summaries that can be checked against the text.
tasks.still_hard: Legal texts need careful wording in summaries.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which ruling changes how the hospital must act.
tasks.altitude: The representative selects and edits instead of scanning and writing.

reach.learn: Whether summaries are clear and timely.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft summaries that can be checked sentence by sentence against the source.
AI Act duties for general systems apply in phases through 2026 and later.

assumptions: Boundary: from new publications to the newsletter shared; policy changes are outside.
Input contract: sources offer alerts; fallback is scanning by hand.
Staff read the newsletter as before.
research_questions: How often does the check drop a sentence?

incremental.description: Patient representative tunes the alert sources.

approvals.approved_version: The newsletter as checked by the representative in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few sources; high: many sources and a regular newsletter.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The patient representative keeps reading, analysing complaints, deciding payment exceptions and selecting risk information; source scanning, tallying, spreadsheet calculations and summaries from scratch shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A representative with more time with patients.
